meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's essay given a zero before anyone called me?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and on what basis?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
Owen drafts elsewhere and pastes it in, like half the school. Did you speak to him before you entered the zero? I'm writing those times down.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Okay. Whatever else happens, nothing goes on his record, and I want that in writing. What else do you have, Hale?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Students misquote Shakespeare all the time, from memory or from a study guide. A wrong line isn't a finding. Show me what else you have.
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
Fine. I've looked at the scene, and I'll check it again at home. So what are you actually proposing for Owen?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their argument between an outline and an essay. That's called drafting. Is there anything else, or is that the lot?

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
Okay. I'll take the rewrite to put this behind him, private, before December 1, replacing the zero, nothing on his record. I want all of it in writing tonight.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth works. Put the time and the room in the email tonight, along with the rest.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen after school on Thursday, November 12, before December 1, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still want the time, the room and every one of those terms confirmed in the same email, and my questions about the outline remain open. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to the private supervised rewrite on Thursday, November 12, with the new mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants all of it confirmed in writing with a time and room; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and her time did not run out first.
What moved her: You turned the laptop and showed the version history with its exact times, because it was dated and she could check it herself.
What cost ground: You never answered whether you spoke to Owen before entering the zero, so her argument about process stayed open to the end.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history showing edits close to midnight on October 28 came near that night, which proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she argued that students change their thesis between an outline and an essay, answer that directly before moving on, for instance by pointing out that the outline's argument and the essay's argument share no ground at all.
